pr_title: Set JWT token to localStorage from cookies
pr_body:
closes https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/47080

I added the JWT to localStorage. Since the Axios interceptor already retrieves the token from localStorage in requests here https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/airflow/ui/src/main.tsx#L50 , I thought it would be a good place to update localStorage after a LoginResponse. This way, subsequent redirects will consider the updated token from localStorage.

Tested:

Login with redirect to connections

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e4f14fae-475e-4a85-bb3b-8f60ec603ca9)

After login redirected to connections page with Authorization header.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/52131827-204f-49b9-a716-3353236ccce7)

> Is there any reason each auth manager has its own login page?

Things like the AWS auth manager might redirect or send to a page elsewhere, so we can't simply have an user/password form that will work for every case.

> Is there any reason each auth manager has its own login page?
>

Yes each auth manager needs to implements its own login mechanism. In the future we might want to implement KeyCloak auth manager. Most likely KeyCloak will have its own login view and we will redirect to that page. You can also imagine some auth manager (most likely private) with no login form, only relying on information from the request (such as LDAP group etc).

issue_context.title: Explore alternatives to putting JWT token in query params
issue_context.body:
### Body

During review of an unrelated PR, it came up that having the JWT token set by putting it into query params is likely not what we want to do - it'll end up in access logs! See [here](https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/47041#discussion_r1970090063).

We should refactor this.



### Committer

review_comments:
## Failure to use secure cookies

Cookie is added without the HttpOnly attribute properly set.

[Show more details](https://github.com/apache/airflow/security/code-scanning/397)
Unfortunately I don't think we can do much here regarding the security warning raised. We can't use httpOnly because we want our JS frontend code to manipulate this...
Yes, we cant do much here, as a security measure at-least we are deleting it from cookies once it consumed to localStorage.
